data.title: Button
data.tagline: Click to save, submit, delete, or run another action
data.description: A button runs an action on the current page, such as saving a form, creating a project, or confirming a deletion. Use a Link to move somewhere else. When several buttons appear together, make the main action easy to spot.

distinctions.label: Segmented control
distinctions.explanation: Button runs an action when clicked. Segmented shows which one of several mutually exclusive options is selected, usually to switch a view or mode.

lessonPractice.title: An account settings page has save profile, discard edits, delete account, and reset password. What is the clearest arrangement?

options.label: Use buttons for save, discard, and delete; keep reset password as a link and confirm deletion
options.feedback: Correct. The first three change or discard current state, while reset password navigates to another page. Deletion also needs confirmation.

options.label: Make save, discard, delete, and reset password all navigation links
options.feedback: Save, discard, and delete act on the current page; links do not express that behavior or handle submission state well.

options.label: Use one Confirm button for every operation and infer the intent afterward
options.feedback: Each action needs an explicit target; destructive account deletion cannot be mixed with routine saving.

data.agentPrompt: Clarify the account settings page: give save profile, discard edits, and delete account their own buttons, with confirmation before delete; keep Reset password as a link. Do not change layout. Trigger save, discard, and delete confirmation, and confirm saving cannot be submitted twice.
